citation.author: Withy, Katherine
citation.title: Finding Oneself, Called
citation.in: Hadjioannou, C. (ed.), Heidegger on Affect, Philosophers in Depth (Palgrave Macmillan) -- Chapter 7 of 12 in a 12-chapter edited collection by 13 distinct authors; Hadjioannou is editor only, not author of this chapter

discipline: philosophy (Heideggerian phenomenology of mind) -- close exegesis of Befindlichkeit in Being and Time, with a brief extension into FCM
thesis: Befindlichkeit ('finding') should not be approached as coextensive with mood: mood is only one ontic expression of a broader disclosive structure that also includes sensing and (as Withy derives) further modes. Finding is equiprimordial with understanding and discoursing and operates on three levels at once -- self-disclosing, world-disclosing, and entity-discovering. To be finding is to find oneself called both by vocations (existentiell identities and, at bottom, the existential vocation of being Dasein) and by the solicitings of entities, where solicitations arise from bringing understanding's possibilities of affording back to Dasein's having-been-thrown.
sections: 1 Existentiell Self-Disclosing: Finding Myself Called to Be Me (pp.154-157) -- identities as vocations; the call delivered by conscience; facticity (Fakten vs. Tatsachen)

2 Existential Self-Disclosing: Finding Oneself Called to Be Dasein (pp.157-162) -- conscience's finding-dimension is angst (SZ 277); Dasein's uncanniness; angst as Grundbefindlichkeit; single-paragraph extension (p.160) identifying profound boredom (FCM 143, 165) as an equivalent ground-finding
3 Discovering: Finding Myself Called by Solicitings (pp.161-162) -- solicitations as a charged subclass of Gibsonian affordances

4 World-Disclosing: Finding the World as a Possibility Space (pp.162-168) -- understanding opens possibilities of affording; finding brings these back to having-been-thrown to open possibilities of soliciting; Table 1 (p.168) summary

5 Modes of Finding (pp.168-174) -- Tables 2-4; extended fear case study; folk-psychological mood/emotion distinction set aside; body argued inessential to finding as such; further modes derived (normative responsiveness, practical usefulness, being-with as loving/dominating, sensing); closes on open questions (p.174)

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: single dense paragraph (p.160): proposes boredom, like angst, can occupy the Grundbefindlichkeit role calling Dasein to the vocation of being Dasein; cites FCM 143 (Anrufen/'the calling') and FCM 165 (the extreme demand); hedged with '(?)' in Table 2 (p.169); full argument deferred to Withy (2013)

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: analogical only, not boredom-specific: practical-usefulness soliciting contrasts feeling capable/confident ('the right tool for the job') against extreme anxiety's overwhelming sense of impossibility and incapacity

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: analogical only: unaffording entities produce distraction, impeding, and irrelevance, correlating with being distracted, frustrated, or indifferent; not connected to boredom in the text

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: essentially absent; one generic remark that finding as such is associated with 'the past', not a boredom-specific time-drag analysis

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: absent; chapter contains no engagement with the psychological state/trait literature

readings.summary: Cites FCM 143's naming of profound boredom's being-held-in-limbo as a 'calling' (Anrufen) in support of the claim that boredom, like angst, is a ground-finding that calls Dasein to the vocation of being Dasein. Not an independent reading of the third form's own structure (Leergelassenheit/Hingehaltenheit not discussed); a single supporting citation for a BT-internal argument about conscience.

Cites FCM 165's 'most extreme demand' -- that Dasein as such is demanded of, and given to, the human being to be there -- as the content of boredom's calling. This passage belongs to FCM's separate 'contemporary Dasein' chapter (secs.37-38); Withy does not otherwise engage that chapter's diagnosis (has man become boring to himself?) or its two-subsection structure.

concepts.gloss: Withy's preferred rendering, replacing 'affectivity' and 'state-of-mind'; the ontological structure of finding oneself situated/attuned, equiprimordial with understanding and discoursing
the ontic expression of Befindlichkeit that Heidegger and most readers treat (mistakenly, per Withy, as the sole expression)
Heidegger's successor to 'consciousness'; the basic way Dasein's 'there' is opened, comprising finding, understanding, and discoursing
ground-finding/ground-mood; the mode of existential vocational finding that discloses the call to be Dasein as such -- angst per BT's official story, extended by Withy to include boredom
an identity that 'speaks' to us and that we are called to take up, rather than a merely available social role
Facts (gender, race, standing, aptitude, body, history) that figure in Dasein's self-interpreting and so function as vocations we must take up, as distinct from mere present-at-hand facts
hearing is understanding's resolute-projecting response to a call; hearkening is finding's moment within conscience -- being open to being addressed
not felt estrangement but the plain structural fact that Dasein can never get behind the ground of its own 'that it is'; what angst authentically discloses
solicitations are a 'charged' subclass of Gibsonian affordances -- entities calling us to engage rather than merely permitting engagement
the network of possible ways entities can be, opened by projecting onto an identity; finding brings these possibilities back to having-been-thrown to produce possibilities of soliciting
the world-disclosing 'slumbering possibility' of being solicited by the threatening, distinct from fearing this or that particular entity

interlocutors: Martin Heidegger (Being and Time, primary target; also cites FCM, History of the Concept of Time [HCT], Metaphysical Foundations of Logic [MFL], Zollikon Seminars [Zo])
James J. Gibson (1986) -- The Theory of Affordances; source of the affordance concept Withy adapts to distinguish affording from soliciting

Matthew Ratcliffe (2013, 2015) -- explicit debt and explicit departure: Withy's world-disclosing interpretation is 'inspired by and indebted to' Ratcliffe's while departing from it significantly (n.6); also disagreed with on whether finding opens practical utility qua affording rather than soliciting (n.12)
Aristotle (Nicomachean Ethics, 1106b, 1115b) -- cited for fear being relative to one's projects/skills rather than to physical strength
William Blattner (2006) -- Heidegger's Being and Time: A Reader's Guide; credited for help understanding the facticity/Fakten point (n.4)
B. Scot Rousse (2018) -- cited for further discussion of self-understanding and das Man in relation to understanding (n.8)
Lauren Freeman (2016) -- 'Defending Heideggerian Mood'; cited as source of the critique that Heidegger's mood account neglects folk-psychological distinctions and the body (n.3)
Matthew Ratcliffe (2013) -- cited alongside Freeman for the same body/folk-psychology critique (n.3)

Katherine Withy (self-citations: 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017a, 2017b) -- prior work on angst's methodological role, FCM's strategic unity, thrownness, uncanniness, and the necessity of present-participle terminology
Mark Okrent and Joe Rouse -- thanked for discussion of the body's role in finding (n.11)
tensions: PRIMARY METHODOLOGICAL AXIS -- mood as the sole/primary ontic expression of finding <-> mood as one among several modes of finding: Withy explicitly rejects approaching Befindlichkeit 'exclusively or even primarily through mood' (p.154), naming sensing (SZ 137) as a second mode and deriving further modes herself in Sec.5 (normative responsiveness, practical usefulness, being-with, sensing-modalities). This is her chapter's central methodological intervention and bears directly on any research design (including Part III's) that would treat mood-report as boredom's sole or exhaustive channel of disclosure.

Angst as BT's sole Grundbefindlichkeit <-> boredom (from FCM) as an equally valid Grundbefindlichkeit for the call to being Dasein: Withy extends the ground-finding role, officially reserved for angst in BT, to profound boredom via FCM 143/165 (p.160), while marking the identification with a hedging '(?)' in her own Table 2 (p.169) and deferring full argument to Withy (2013). This corroborates, from a different route, the debate axis bor-sec-02 explicitly flagged and left open ('anxiety vs. profound boredom as candidate Grundstimmung').

Understanding as world-disclosing / finding as entity-discovering (a 'clean division of labor' reading) <-> Withy's own claim that each of finding and understanding discloses the self, discloses the world, AND discovers entities (Sec.3, p.162): she explicitly rejects the simpler division-of-labor reading some might infer from Heidegger's own examples.

Body as essential to any adequate account of mood/affectivity (implicit in Freeman 2016 and Ratcliffe 2013's critiques, n.3) <-> body as inessential to finding-as-such, though possibly essential to specific ontic modes like sensing (pp.171-172): Withy argues Heidegger's 'neglect' of the body is 'no neglect at all' so far as finding proper is concerned.

Ratcliffe's reading that finding opens practical utility qua the affording <-> Withy's own reading that practical utility is itself a soliciting, not a mere affording (p.172 n.12) -- an explicit, narrow scholarly disagreement.
